messages:
lina: FYI partner flagged degraded throughput + sporadic `illegal memory access` on H100s after vendor pushed an image with NVIDIA driver 542.6 + CUDA 12.4. This is impacting joint marketplace offering (throughput down ~40%). Link: https://partner.example.com/tickets/9802

devon: Any logs/snippet? which model config and batch sizes?

lina: Partner supplied snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-21T09:05:02Z] runtime ERROR: cuMemcpyAsync H2D failed: unspecified launch failure
[2026-03-21T09:05:02Z] runtime WARN: kernel returned illegal memory access, falling back to safe path
[2026-03-21T09:05:02Z] worker ERROR: inference failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
```
They run a quantized 7B family with dynamic KV cache, batches 2-8.

priya: We reproduced on our integration fleet using the vendor image. Failures cluster on particular H100 firmware variants. A100s fine so far.

igor: Observed behavior suggests newer driver changes kernel launch validation and tighter checks; some custom kernels in our fused op set trigger illegal-address aborts. Could be kernel-build flags + driver ABI mismatch.

devon: Short term: can marketplace pin back to last stable driver (540.2) for the joint listing only? We should avoid global rollback.

marketplace-bot: Marketplace image update queued: set driver_pin=540.2 for listing 'partner-x-llm-v2' (acting on devon request). ETA ~4h for canary rollout.

priya: I'll run an expanded matrix across H100 firmware + drivers (540, 542) and post failure rates tonight. Also adding kernel-dispatch trace to isolate which fused op misbehaves.

igor: Mid-term: runtime should detect illegal-address-prone kernels and prefer non-fused fallback on drivers >=542 until we can rebuild kernels with driver-safe flags. I'll open a runtime PR with a guarded fallback (limit fused-kernel execution on suspect driver).

devon: Action plan (concise):
- devon: coordinate partner pin and confirm canary (ETA 4h)
- priya: run driver/firmware matrix on H100 + post logs (ETA tonight)
- igor: open PR 'fix/guard-fused-kernels-driver-542' with runtime guard + test (ETA 36h)
- lina: send partner-facing note: pining + investigative work, no public comms yet (ETA 2h)
- eng-ops: add driver-version + firmware to incident template for marketplace listings (ETA 24h)

eng-ops: Noted, will add fields and a checklist: driver_version, cuda_runtime, gpu_firmware, image_tag, kernel-build-id.

lina: Partner asked if ROCm side has similar risk for private deployments (they want to expand to on-prem SGX). priya: we haven't seen ROCm issues in our internal matrix but we'll add ROCm 5.8 and 5.10 tests for parity.

devon: Partner requested an SLA-friendly mitigation: a marketplace toggle to pin driver per-listing + an API to trigger immediate rollback. marketplace-bot: adding an API work item in backlog.

marketplace-bot: New incident created: INC-2026-291 (marketplace-driver-compat). Assigned: partnerships, eng-runtime, marketplace.

lina: Draft partner message: "We've pinned your marketplace listing to driver 540.2 while we validate fixes. We're running an expanded hardware+driver matrix and will share results tonight. We'll only rollback the listing if your canary results are green; no public announcement until we confirm root cause."

igor: For postmortem: capture a reproducible kernel trace, kernel-build flags, and exact driver+firmware combo. Also recommend adding a nightly job: marketplace-gate runs `runtime-smoke --driver X --fw Y --model tiny-7b` against new vendor images.

priya: I'll attach the first round of logs here once matrix finishes (will include `dmesg`, driver ABI reports, and `nvprof` traces).

lina: Good. Keep updates in this thread. If partner escalates externally, I'll handle external comms and coordinate with legal/marketing.
